descripcion_geo: Roman province in southern Greece, with Corinth as its capital. Intellectual and commercial center of the Hellenistic world.
importancia_estrategica: Province where Paul founded the church of Corinth and was related to Athens.

historias.titulo: Paul in Achaia: Athens and Corinth
historias.descripcion: Paul preached in the Areopagus in Athens and then founded the church in Corinth, capital of Achaia, where he remained for 18 months.

historias.titulo: The collection for the saints of Jerusalem in Achaia
historias.descripcion: Paul praises the generosity of Achaia (Corinth) in Jerusalem's collection for the poor.
The proconsul Gallio rejects the Jews' accusation against Paul, stating that it is a matter of their own law.

personajes.descripcion: He founded the church of Corinth in Achaia; he wrote the letters to the Corinthians from and for this region.
He rejected the accusation against Paul; his command serves as the chronological anchor of the NT.
Converted by Paul into Achaia; His conversion was a sign of the power of the gospel.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Intellectual and moral center of the Greco-Roman world; The letters to the Corinthians reveal the challenges of the gospel in a cosmopolitan pagan city.

cristianismo.descripcion: Paul presents the gospel at the philosophical center of the world; The 'unknown God' that the Athenians worshiped is the one that Paul announces.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: Paul presents the gospel at the philosophical center of the world; The 'unknown God' that the Athenians worshiped is the one that Paul announces.

historias.titulo: Paul in the Areopagus of Athens
historias.descripcion: Paul presents the gospel to the Stoic and Epicurean philosophers at the Areopagus; some believe.

historias.titulo: The founding of the Corinthian church
historias.descripcion: Paul spends 18 months in Corinth founding a community in the heart of Achaia.

historias.titulo: The Epistles to the Corinthians: Theology for an Urban Church
historias.descripcion: Paul writes two letters to the Corinthian church addressing morality, spiritual gifts, and the resurrection.

personajes.descripcion: He founded the church of Corinth; his letters to the Corinthians are central to the NT.
Judeo-Christian couple who welcomed Paul in Corinth.
One of the few converts from the Areopagus speech; Tradition makes him the first bishop of Athens.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Achaia was the first proper Greek soil where the gospel took deep roots.

cristianismo.descripcion: The altar to the 'Unknown God' in Athens gave Paul the bridge to announce the Creator God to the Greek intellectual world.
cristianismo.significado_teologico: The altar to the 'Unknown God' in Athens gave Paul the bridge to announce the Creator God to the Greek intellectual world.
